## Method and limits
- **Window:** 2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01 exclusive, so the last full month is 2026-05. Today is 2026-10-23, so the data ends about 145 days before today (derived). Nothing after May 2026 is covered.
- **Lane:** news only, monthly granularity. No research or other lanes were used.
- **Coverage:** the news table passed strict index partition reads and historical row floors, at 107.1% of the expected row count [c1]. The tool describes this as a reachability check, not proof that ingest is complete.
- **Censoring:** the tool censors the newest month because ingest lags publication [c1]. All 24 months are flagged `partial_period: false` [c1].
- **Match mode:** not stated in the response. Terms appear to be matched as keywords. The tool warns that a term that is also a common word will over-count [c1]. "Russia" and "Ukraine" are unlikely to be ambiguous, but this is untested here.
- **What the counts are:**
  - Counts are articles mentioning each term, which is attention.
  - Counts are not importance, accuracy or audience reach [c1].
  - Shares are shares of the summed counts. An article naming several terms is counted once per term, so the 2,348,614 combined figure [c1] is not a count of distinct articles.
  - The overlap is unmeasured here (see f5).
- **Not answerable from this data:**
  - Why coverage moved.
  - Which outlets or countries drive it.
  - Tone toward each entity, as opposed to tone of articles that mention it.
  - Classifier accuracy.
  - The formulas for growth, tone_ratio and vs_baseline.
- **Interpretation:** I inferred the tone_ratio direction (negative per positive) and the reading of the NATO rise as a distinct storyline. Everything else is arithmetic on [c1].
